title: Games & Computational Thinking
summary: The goal of the first year is to have fun and learn how computers 'think' through physical games, puzzles and robotics. The focus is on understanding sequences and cause-and-effect before moving to screens.

semesters.title: Games for Computational Thinking
materials: Board games (Mastermind, Decrypto, Robot Turtles, etc.)
learningOutcomes: Understand sequences, patterns, and cause-and-effect.
Develop clear step-by-step instructions to parallel algorithmic programming.
semesters.description: Students explore the foundations of computational thinking through board and card games.

semesters.title: Robots & Visual Programming
learningOutcomes: Programming physical robots to follow paths and commands
Understanding sequences and loops through physical movement
Debugging robotic behaviors by observing physical outputs
semesters.description: Students get hands-on with educational robots, learning to program physical devices using visual codes and commands.

title: Computers and Simple Programming
summary: The small, single-board Raspberry Pi computer is introduced. Students learn to code using the drag-and-drop interface of Scratch. In semester 2, they graduate to text-based programming using Python to control simple electronic circuits with LEDs and motors.

semesters.title: Programming with Scratch
learningOutcomes: Introduction to the Raspberry Pi environment
Creating interactive stories and games using Scratch
Understanding basic programming concepts like loops, events, and variables
semesters.description: Students take their first steps into programming using Scratch. They learn how to build interactive stories and games, developing their algorithmic thinking and problem-solving skills in a visual environment.

semesters.title: Programming Electronics with Python
learningOutcomes: Transitioning from visual blocks to text-based Python programming
Using Python to control LEDs (blink, flash patterns) and simple motors (for basic robotics)
Introduction to timing, loops, and conditional logic in Python
semesters.description: Building on their initial programming experience, students transition to Python, a widely used text-based language. They learn to write scripts that interact with the physical world, controlling LEDs and motors. This bridges the gap between software logic and hardware control.

title: Phone Specific Components
summary: A wide range of smartphone specific inputs and outputs are introduced. This builds familiarity with the components on a modern smartphone and lays the groundwork for understanding how we interact with these devices and the type of data created.

semesters.title: Inputs
learningOutcomes: Replace simple switches with touch, motion and light sensors.
Record and analyze audio input from the microphone
Capture and process images from the camera
Detecting tilt and shake gestures
semesters.description: An array of sensors which provide inputs to a computer are introduced. Students learn how to read data from these sensors and use it to create interactive projects that respond to touch, motion, light, sound, and images.

semesters.title: Outputs & Power
learningOutcomes: Use a touchscreen display to create interactive user interfaces
Generating audio output through speakers for alerts and media playback
Understanding battery technology and power management for portable devices.
semesters.description: Students shift focus to the output capabilities of mobile devices, learning how to present information visually and audibly. They will also explore power management, understanding how batteries work and how to efficiently power their portable projects.

title: Connectivity: Wi-Fi & Bluetooth
summary: The device connects to the world as students explore the invisible networks that link computers. Practical exercises involve scanning for networks and sending messages between devices.

semesters.title: Wireless Networks & Servers
learningOutcomes: Understanding radio waves
Scanning for Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth devices using the Pi
Setting up a simple web server on the Pi
Accessing a custom webpage from another device on the same network
semesters.description: In this semester, students will explore wireless networks & servers, building on concepts from previous modules.

semesters.title: Bluetooth Communication & IoT
learningOutcomes: Pairing devices and sending simple text strings between them over Bluetooth
Controlling the LEDs/Motors from a smartphone browser over the local Wi-Fi network
semesters.description: In this semester, students will explore bluetooth communication & iot, building on concepts from previous modules.

title: Putting It All Together
summary: The final hardware component—the cellular modem—transforms the computer into a true mobile phone. Students learn how cellular networks function and write scripts to send SMS and make calls.

semesters.title: Cellular Hardware & Communication
learningOutcomes: What is a Subscriber Identity Module? Connecting a 4G HAT and inserting a SIM
Communicating directly with the modem using standard AT commands
checking signal strength and network status
semesters.description: In this semester, students will explore cellular hardware & communication, building on concepts from previous modules.

semesters.title: SMS & Voice Integration
learningOutcomes: Writing a script to send and receive text messages programmatically
Initiating a voice call through the Pi
Routing audio to the microphone and speaker
semesters.description: In this semester, students will explore sms & voice integration, building on concepts from previous modules.
